claim: High-level protection in humans can be achieved by experimental immunization with Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites attenuated by radiation.
source: High-level protection in humans can be achieved by experimental immunization with Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites attenuated by radiation or under anti-malarial drug coverage.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Clyde et al., 1973; Hoffman et al., 2002) demonstrating this finding.

claim: High-level protection in humans can be achieved by experimental immunization with Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites under anti-malarial drug coverage.
source: High-level protection in humans can be achieved by experimental immunization with Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites attenuated by radiation or under anti-malarial drug coverage.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Roestenberg et al., 2009, 2011) demonstrating this finding.

claim: PbΔb9ΔslarpGAP was completely attenuated showing no breakthrough infections in the rodent malaria model.
source: In the rodent malaria model, PbΔb9ΔslarpGAP was completely attenuated showing no breakthrough infections while efficiently inducing high-level protection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2 showing no breakthrough blood infections after injection of PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites.

claim: PbΔb9ΔslarpGAP efficiently induced high-level protection in the rodent malaria model.
source: In the rodent malaria model, PbΔb9ΔslarpGAP was completely attenuated showing no breakthrough infections while efficiently inducing high-level protection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing protection of mice after immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites.

claim: The human PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP were generated without drug resistance markers.
source: The human PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP generated without drug resistance markers were infective to human hepatocytes in vitro and to humanized mice engrafted with human hepatocytes in vivo but completely aborted development after infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the FRT/FLPe recombinase methodology used to remove drug resistance markers from the genome.

claim: PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP were infective to human hepatocytes in vitro.
source: The human PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP generated without drug resistance markers were infective to human hepatocytes in vitro and to humanized mice engrafted with human hepatocytes in vivo but completely aborted development after infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A demonstrating invasion of primary human hepatocytes by PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites.

claim: PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP were infective to humanized mice engrafted with human hepatocytes in vivo.
source: The human PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP generated without drug resistance markers were infective to human hepatocytes in vitro and to humanized mice engrafted with human hepatocytes in vivo but completely aborted development after infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D demonstrating infection of humanized mice by PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites.

claim: PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP completely aborted development after infection of human hepatocytes.
source: The human PfΔb9ΔslarpGAP generated without drug resistance markers were infective to human hepatocytes in vitro and to humanized mice engrafted with human hepatocytes in vivo but completely aborted development after infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D demonstrating lack of parasite development in human hepatocytes and humanized mice.

claim: A vaccine that induces high-level (>90%) sterile protection by inducing immunity that attacks the pre-erythrocytic stages of Plasmodium falciparum will prevent infection, disease, and transmission.
source: A vaccine that induces high-level (>90%) sterile protection by inducing immunity that attacks the non-pathologic, asymptomatic pre-erythrocytic stages of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) will prevent infection, disease, and transmission and could be a powerful instrument to eliminate Pf malaria from geographically defined areas (Plowe et al., 2009; malERA Consultative Group on Vaccines, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Plowe et al., 2009; malERA Consultative Group on Vaccines, 2011) discussing this concept.

claim: A pre-erythrocytic stage vaccine could be a powerful instrument to eliminate Pf malaria from geographically defined areas.
source: A vaccine that induces high-level (>90%) sterile protection by inducing immunity that attacks the non-pathologic, asymptomatic pre-erythrocytic stages of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) will prevent infection, disease, and transmission and could be a powerful instrument to eliminate Pf malaria from geographically defined areas (Plowe et al., 2009; malERA Consultative Group on Vaccines, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Plowe et al., 2009; malERA Consultative Group on Vaccines, 2011) discussing this concept.

claim: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites attenuated by irradiation.
source: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites attenuated by either irradiation, genetic modification (GAP), or by concomitant anti-parasitic drug treatment (For reviews see Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to review articles (Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).

claim: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites attenuated by genetic modification (GAP).
source: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites attenuated by either irradiation, genetic modification (GAP), or by concomitant anti-parasitic drug treatment (For reviews see Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to review articles (Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).

claim: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites with concomitant anti-parasitic drug treatment.
source: In rodent models, sterile protection can be induced by immunization with live Plasmodium sporozoites attenuated by either irradiation, genetic modification (GAP), or by concomitant anti-parasitic drug treatment (For reviews see Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to review articles (Hoffman et al., 2010; Butler et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).

claim: Complete sustained protective immunity against a challenge infection has been achieved in humans by exposure to the bites of mosquitoes infected with live radiation-attenuated Plasmodium sporozoites that invade but then completely arrest in the liver.
source: In humans, induction of complete sustained protective immunity against a challenge infection has been achieved by previous exposure to the bites of mosquitoes infected with i) live radiation-attenuated Plasmodium sporozoites that invade but then completely arrest in the liver (Clyde et al., 1973; Hoffman et al., 2002) and ii) live sporozoites in volunteers taking chloroquine chemoprophylaxis (CPS) with full parasite liver-stage development; once released into the circulation asexual blood stages are killed by chloroquine (Roestenberg et al., 2009, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Clyde et al., 1973; Hoffman et al., 2002) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Complete sustained protective immunity against a challenge infection has been achieved in humans by exposure to live sporozoites in volunteers taking chloroquine chemoprophylaxis (CPS) with full parasite liver-stage development.
source: In humans, induction of complete sustained protective immunity against a challenge infection has been achieved by previous exposure to the bites of mosquitoes infected with i) live radiation-attenuated Plasmodium sporozoites that invade but then completely arrest in the liver (Clyde et al., 1973; Hoffman et al., 2002) and ii) live sporozoites in volunteers taking chloroquine chemoprophylaxis (CPS) with full parasite liver-stage development; once released into the circulation asexual blood stages are killed by chloroquine (Roestenberg et al., 2009, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Roestenberg et al., 2009, 2011) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Sterile immunity can be achieved by intravenous immunization with radiation-attenuated aseptic, purified, cryopreserved Pf sporozoites (SPZ) called PfSPZ Vaccine.
source: More recently it has been demonstrated for the first time that sterile immunity can be achieved by intravenous immunization with radiation-attenuated aseptic, purified, cryopreserved Pf sporozoites (SPZ) called PfSPZ Vaccine (Seder et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Seder et al., 2013) demonstrating this finding.

claim: GAPs have the advantage of representing a homogeneous parasite population with a defined genetic identity from a product manufacturing perspective.
source: From a product manufacturing perspective, GAPs have the clear advantage of representing a homogeneous parasite population with a defined genetic identity.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference about the properties of genetically attenuated parasites.

claim: The genetic attenuation is an irreversible, intrinsic characteristic of the parasite that does not require additional manufacturing steps like irradiation.
source: The genetic attenuation is an irreversible, intrinsic characteristic of the parasite that does not require additional manufacturing steps like irradiation.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about genetic modifications being permanent changes to the genome.

claim: In the manufacturing process of GAP-infected mosquitoes, operators are never exposed to Pf parasites that can cause disease.
source: Furthermore, in the manufacturing process of GAP-infected mosquitoes, operators are never exposed to Pf parasites that can cause disease.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference that attenuated parasites cannot cause disease.

claim: Clinical development of GAPs has suffered from safety problems related to breakthrough infections during immunization leading to pathological blood stage infections.
source: However, clinical development of GAPs has suffered from safety problems related to breakthrough infections during immunization leading to pathological blood stage infections responsible for clinical symptoms and complications.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Spring et al., 2013) demonstrating breakthrough infections in a clinical trial.

claim: Strains of mice showed differential susceptibility to breakthrough infections after injection of sporozoites of rodent malaria GAPs.
source: Strains of mice showed differential susceptibility to breakthrough infections after injection of sporozoites of rodent malaria GAPs, demonstrating the need for extensive preclinical rodent screening (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012) demonstrating this finding.

claim: The P. falciparum GAP PfΔp52Δp36 is the only GAP so far that has been assessed in humans.
source: The P. falciparum GAP PfΔp52Δp36 is the only GAP so far that has been assessed in humans but the trial in which the Pf sporozoites were administered by mosquito bite had to be terminated, because of breakthrough infections in one volunteer during immunization (Spring et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Spring et al., 2013) describing the clinical trial.

claim: The trial with PfΔp52Δp36 had to be terminated because of breakthrough infections in one volunteer during immunization.
source: The P. falciparum GAP PfΔp52Δp36 is the only GAP so far that has been assessed in humans but the trial in which the Pf sporozoites were administered by mosquito bite had to be terminated, because of breakthrough infections in one volunteer during immunization (Spring et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Spring et al., 2013) describing the clinical trial termination.

claim: In vitro experiments with PfΔp52Δp36 confirm that this double gene deletion GAP is not fully attenuated.
source: Our in vitro experiments with PfΔp52Δp36 confirm that this double gene deletion GAP (i.e. two genes removed from the genome) is not fully attenuated similar to the equivalent rodent GAP PbΔp52Δp36 in the Plasmodium berghei/C57BL/6 model (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' own experimental data and citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012).

claim: The equivalent rodent GAP PbΔp52Δp36 is not fully attenuated in the Plasmodium berghei/C57BL/6 model.
source: Our in vitro experiments with PfΔp52Δp36 confirm that this double gene deletion GAP (i.e. two genes removed from the genome) is not fully attenuated similar to the equivalent rodent GAP PbΔp52Δp36 in the Plasmodium berghei/C57BL/6 model (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Identification of additional genes critical and uniquely selective for liver-stage development has become a major challenge for GAP vaccine development.
source: Therefore, identification of additional genes critical and uniquely selective for liver-stage development has become a major challenge for GAP vaccine development (Annoura et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Ploemen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012; Khan et al., 2012; Ploemen et al., 2012) discussing this challenge.

claim: Single gene deletion GAPs will most likely not be adequate.
source: Furthermore, single gene deletion GAPs will most likely not be adequate (Ploemen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Ploemen et al., 2012) discussing this conclusion.

claim: B9 protein is a newly identified member of the Plasmodium 6-Cys family of proteins.
source: This protein is a newly identified member of the Plasmodium 6-Cys family of proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) identifying B9 as a 6-Cys family member.

claim: PbΔb9 mutants have a stronger attenuation phenotype than mutants lacking the 6-Cys proteins P52 and P36.
source: Initial safety evaluation in rodents demonstrated that PbΔb9 mutants have a stronger attenuation phenotype than mutants lacking the 6-Cys proteins P52 and P36 (van Dijk et al., 2005; van Schaijk et al., 2008; VanBuskirk et al., 2009; Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (van Dijk et al., 2005; van Schaijk et al., 2008; VanBuskirk et al., 2009; Annoura et al., 2014) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Rodent sporozoites lacking slarp show an excellent safety profile by full arrest in the liver in mice.
source: These slarp mutants show an excellent safety profile by full arrest in the liver in mice (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008) demonstrating this finding.

claim: The SLARP protein is expressed in sporozoites and in early liver-stages.
source: The SLARP protein is expressed in sporozoites and in early liver-stages and is involved in the regulation of transcription (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011) demonstrating this finding.

claim: The SLARP protein is involved in the regulation of transcription.
source: The SLARP protein is expressed in sporozoites and in early liver-stages and is involved in the regulation of transcription (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011) demonstrating this finding.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp was generated using constructs that allowed for the removal of the drug selectable marker from the genome by FRT/FLPe recombinase methodology.
source: PfΔb9Δslarp was generated using constructs that allowed for the removal of the drug selectable marker from the genome by FRT/FLPe recombinase methodology (van Schaijk et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (van Schaijk et al., 2010) describing this methodology and by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Liver-stage development of PbΔb9 was fully abrogated in BALB/c mice.
source: Characterization of the PbΔb9 phenotype showed that liver-stage development was fully abrogated in BALB/c mice and severely compromised in the more stringent C57BL/6 murine model for P. berghei (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Liver-stage development of PbΔb9 was severely compromised in the C57BL/6 murine model for P. berghei.
source: Characterization of the PbΔb9 phenotype showed that liver-stage development was fully abrogated in BALB/c mice and severely compromised in the more stringent C57BL/6 murine model for P. berghei (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) demonstrating this finding.

claim: Immunization of a single dose of 10k PbΔb9 protected BALB/c mice against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge.
source: Immunization of a single dose of 10k (i.e. 10,000 sporozoites) or 5k PbΔb9 protected BALB/c mice against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge, while 80% of mice were still protected after a single 1k immunizing dose (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: Immunization of a single dose of 5k PbΔb9 protected BALB/c mice against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge.
source: Immunization of a single dose of 10k (i.e. 10,000 sporozoites) or 5k PbΔb9 protected BALB/c mice against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge, while 80% of mice were still protected after a single 1k immunizing dose (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: 80% of BALB/c mice were protected after a single 1k immunizing dose of PbΔb9 against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge.
source: Immunization of a single dose of 10k (i.e. 10,000 sporozoites) or 5k PbΔb9 protected BALB/c mice against a 10k WT-sporozoite challenge, while 80% of mice were still protected after a single 1k immunizing dose (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 8/10 mice protected.

claim: In C57BL/6 mice, immunization with 50K/20K/20K of PbΔb9 resulted in complete protection lasting up to 180 days.
source: In C57BL/6 mice, immunization with 50K/20K/20K of PbΔb9 resulted in complete protection lasting up to 180 days, reducing to 45% protection when challenged at 1 year post-immunization.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: Protection in C57BL/6 mice immunized with 50K/20K/20K of PbΔb9 reduced to 45% when challenged at 1 year post-immunization.
source: In C57BL/6 mice, immunization with 50K/20K/20K of PbΔb9 resulted in complete protection lasting up to 180 days, reducing to 45% protection when challenged at 1 year post-immunization.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 5/11 mice protected at day 365.

claim: Sporozoite administration of PbΔb9 occasionally resulted in blood stage infections after administration of high doses.
source: However, sporozoite administration occasionally resulted in blood stage infections after administration of high doses, thereby compromising the safety profile (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) demonstrating this finding.

claim: PbΔslarp parasites are completely arrested in liver-stage development with a complete lack of breakthrough blood-stage infections.
source: Previously, it has been shown by others that PbΔslarp parasites are completely arrested in liver-stage development with a complete lack of breakthrough blood-stage infections (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008) demonstrating this finding.

claim: The PbΔslarp mutant showed blood stage growth and mosquito infections with functional sporozoites similar to wild-type.
source: The PbΔslarp mutant showed blood stage growth and mosquito infections with functional sporozoites similar to wild-type (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Intravenous injection of up to 500k PbΔslarp sporozoites never led to full development of parasites in the liver.
source: However, intravenous injection of up to 500k PbΔslarp sporozoites never led to full development of parasites in the liver as assayed by in vivo imaging (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) or analysis of blood stage infection (Table 2).

claim: PbΔslarp sporozoites arrested very soon after invasion of cultured Huh7 hepatocytes.
source: PbΔslarp sporozoites arrested very soon after invasion of cultured Huh7 hepatocytes corroborating the excellent safety findings by Silvie et al. (2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior work (Silvie et al., 2008).

claim: PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites arrested soon after invasion of cultured Huh7 hepatocytes.

claim: Intravenous injection of 150–200K PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites never resulted in breakthrough blood-stage infections in mice.
source: However, PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites arrested soon after invasion of cultured Huh7 hepatocytes (Figure 1) and intravenous injection of 150–200K PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites never resulted in breakthrough blood-stage infections in mice (Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: A single immunization dose of 10K PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge.
source: A single immunization dose of 10K, 5K, or even 1K of PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 20/20 mice protected.

claim: A single immunization dose of 5K PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge.
source: A single immunization dose of 10K, 5K, or even 1K of PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 10/10 mice protected.

claim: A single immunization dose of 1K PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge.
source: A single immunization dose of 10K, 5K, or even 1K of PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites in BALB/c mice induced full protection against a 10K wild-type sporozoite challenge (Table 1).

claim: C57BL/6 mice were 100% protected after 3 × 10K immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites.

claim: The protective efficacy in C57BL/6 mice reduced to 60% after a 3 × 1K immunization dose of PbΔb9Δslarp.
source: C57BL/6 mice were 100% protected after 3 × 10K immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites, and the protective efficacy reduced to 60% after a 3 × 1K immunization dose.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 6/10 mice protected.

claim: A challenge at day 180 post-immunization of a 50/20/20K dose of PbΔb9Δslarp still resulted in complete protection in C57BL/6 mice.
source: A challenge at day 180 post-immunization of a 50/20/20K dose still resulted in complete protection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1 showing 6/6 mice protected.

claim: PbΔb9Δslarp completely arrest during liver-stage development.
source: The combined data showed that PbΔb9Δslarp completely arrest during liver-stage development and induce a highly efficient protective immunity in two different strains of mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2 and Figure 1.

claim: PbΔb9Δslarp induce a highly efficient protective immunity in two different strains of mice.
source: The combined data showed that PbΔb9Δslarp completely arrest during liver-stage development and induce a highly efficient protective immunity in two different strains of mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: Pfb9 shows 37% amino acid sequence identity with Pbb9.
source: Pfb9 shows 37% amino acid sequence identity and 54% sequence similarity with Pbb9 ((Annoura et al., 2014)); Pfslarp shows 28% amino acid sequence identity and 46% sequence similarity with Pbslarp.

claim: Pfb9 shows 54% sequence similarity with Pbb9.
source: Pfb9 shows 37% amino acid sequence identity and 54% sequence similarity with Pbb9 ((Annoura et al., 2014)); Pfslarp shows 28% amino acid sequence identity and 46% sequence similarity with Pbslarp.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) and sequence analysis.

claim: Pfslarp shows 28% amino acid sequence identity with Pbslarp.
source: Pfb9 shows 37% amino acid sequence identity and 54% sequence similarity with Pbb9 ((Annoura et al., 2014)); Pfslarp shows 28% amino acid sequence identity and 46% sequence similarity with Pbslarp.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis.

claim: Pfslarp shows 46% sequence similarity with Pbslarp.
source: Pfb9 shows 37% amino acid sequence identity and 54% sequence similarity with Pbb9 ((Annoura et al., 2014)); Pfslarp shows 28% amino acid sequence identity and 46% sequence similarity with Pbslarp.

claim: Blood-stage development of two independently derived PfΔslarp parasites was comparable to WT parasites.
source: Blood-stage development of two independently derived PfΔslarp (i.e. PfΔslarp-a and–b) parasites was comparable to WT parasites.

claim: PfΔslarp mutants produced WT numbers of gametocytes, oocysts and sporozoites.
source: PfΔslarp mutants produced WT numbers of gametocytes, oocysts and sporozoites (Figure 2).

claim: The intra-cellular PfΔslarp-a and -b parasite development in primary human hepatocytes was not significantly different in number and morphologically identical to WT parasites at 3 and 24 hours post-infection.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: The number of PfΔslarp parasites in primary human hepatocytes was more than 10-fold reduced at 48 hpi compared to WT.
source: However, their number was more than 10-fold reduced at 48 hpi and not detectable from day 3 onwards to day 7 post-infection.

claim: PfΔslarp parasites were not detectable from day 3 onwards to day 7 post-infection in primary human hepatocytes.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Parasites lacking b9 in P. falciparum arrested before day 2 post-infection of primary human hepatocytes with the exception of one observed liver schizont at a later timepoint.

evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) demonstrating this finding.

claim: PfΔslarp-a and -b parasites still showed positive HSP70 staining and morphologically normal parasites at 48 hpi in primary human hepatocytes.

claim: The time point of arrest for PfΔslarp parasites is later compared to PfΔb9 parasites.

claim: Asexual blood stage growth of PfΔb9Δslarp parasites was normal.

claim: Both PfΔb9Δslarp clones reached an asexual parasitemia between 0.5 and 5% during cloning within 21 days.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp clones produced WT-like numbers of gametocytes, oocysts, and sporozoites.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed normal hepatic cell traversal.
source: PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed normal gliding motility, hepatic cell traversal (Figure 2), as well as invasion of primary human hepatocytes, but parasites were completely absent in two independent experiments at day 2 up to day 7 post-infection, following inoculation of primary human hepatocytes with 40,000 PfΔb9Δslarp F7 or G9 sporozoites (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed normal invasion of primary human hepatocytes.
source: PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed normal gliding motility, hepatic cell traversal (Figure 2), as well as invasion of primary human hepatocytes, but parasites were completely absent in two independent experiments at day 2 up to day 7 post-infection, following inoculation of primary human hepatocytes with 40,000 PfΔb9Δslarp F7 or G9 sporozoites (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp parasites were completely absent in two independent experiments at day 2 up to day 7 post-infection, following inoculation of primary human hepatocytes with 40,000 PfΔb9Δslarp F7 or G9 sporozoites.
source: PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed normal gliding motility, hepatic cell traversal (Figure 2), as well as invasion of primary human hepatocytes, but parasites were completely absent in two independent experiments at day 2 up to day 7 post-infection, following inoculation of primary human hepatocytes with 40,000 PfΔb9Δslarp F7 or G9 sporozoites (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Detailed analyses of 80 individual wells at day 4 post-infection did not result in identification of a single developing PfΔb9Δslarp parasite.
source: Detailed analyses of 80 individual wells at day 4 post-infection did not result in identification of a single developing parasite.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The timing of arrest for PfΔb9Δslarp is similar to PfΔb9.
source: The combined day 2 and day 4 data of PfΔb9Δslarp indicated that the timing of arrest is similar to PfΔb9 (Annoura et al., 2014) and there had been complete arrest of liver-stage development, similar to PfΔslarp parasites.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data and citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014).

claim: There had been complete arrest of liver-stage development for PfΔb9Δslarp, similar to PfΔslarp parasites.
source: The combined day 2 and day 4 data of PfΔb9Δslarp indicated that the timing of arrest is similar to PfΔb9 (Annoura et al., 2014) and there had been complete arrest of liver-stage development, similar to PfΔslarp parasites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Both mice infected with WT Pf and 1 of the 2 mice infected with PfΔb9Δslarp were positive for Pf 18S DNA at 24 hr post-infection in human liver-uPA-SCID mice.
source: Both mice infected with WT Pf and 1 of the 2 mice infected with PfΔb9Δslarp were positive for Pf 18S DNA at 24 hr post-infection, demonstrating successful sporozoite infection in human hepatocytes (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: A lower signal was observed in PfΔb9Δslarp-infected mice at day 1 after infection compared to WT parasites.
source: A lower signal was observed in PfΔb9Δslarp-infected mice at day 1 after infection compared to WT parasites, likely reflecting the early time point of arrest of this GAP.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The lower signal in PfΔb9Δslarp-infected mice at day 1 likely reflects the early time point of arrest of this GAP.
source: A lower signal was observed in PfΔb9Δslarp-infected mice at day 1 after infection compared to WT parasites, likely reflecting the early time point of arrest of this GAP.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data.

claim: All mice infected with Pf WT (3/3) showed a strong increase in parasite 18S DNA at day 5 post-infection, representing successful liver-stage development.
source: All mice infected with Pf WT (3/3) showed a strong increase in parasite 18S DNA at day 5 post-infection, representing successful liver-stage development.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: None of the human liver-uPA-SCID mice infected with PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed 18S DNA higher than heterozygous uPA+/−-SCID mice at day 5 post-infection.
source: In contrast, none of the human liver-uPA-SCID mice infected with PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites showed 18S DNA higher than heterozygous uPA+/−-SCID mice, not engrafted with human hepatocytes that had been infected with PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp parasites can invade but do not develop in livers of humanized mice.
source: Although these studies were performed with a limited number of mice, these findings indicate that PfΔb9Δslarp parasites can invade but do not develop in livers of humanized mice.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp demonstrates abrogation of development inside human hepatocytes.
source: Our combined results demonstrate abrogation of development of PfΔb9Δslarp inside human hepatocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The rodent GAP PbΔb9Δslarp completely arrested early in liver-stage development in two different mouse strains after injection of very high number of sporozoites.
source: The rodent GAP PbΔb9Δslarp completely arrested early in liver-stage development in two different mouse strains after injection of very high number of sporozoites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: Immunizations with PbΔb9Δslarp efficiently induced sterile and long-lasting protective immunity in both BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice.
source: In addition, immunizations with PbΔb9Δslarp efficiently induced sterile and long-lasting protective immunity in both BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: The Pf GAP PfΔslarpΔb9 completely aborted development in human hepatocytes 1 day after invasion.
source: Similarly, the Pf GAP PfΔslarpΔb9 completely aborted development in human hepatocytes 1 day after invasion, while sporozoites were fully motile and invasive with infectivity comparable to Pf WT sporozoites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: PfΔslarpΔb9 sporozoites were fully motile and invasive with infectivity comparable to Pf WT sporozoites.
source: Similarly, the Pf GAP PfΔslarpΔb9 completely aborted development in human hepatocytes 1 day after invasion, while sporozoites were fully motile and invasive with infectivity comparable to Pf WT sporozoites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 3A.

claim: Asexual parasite growth and production of salivary gland sporozoites in the mosquito were unaffected for PfΔb9Δslarp.
source: Importantly, asexual parasite growth and production of salivary gland sporozoites in the mosquito were unaffected ensuring normal GAP production.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PbΔb9Δslarp is the first completely attenuated rodent mutant in which multiple genes have been deleted that are critical for two independent biological processes during liver-stage development.
source: PbΔb9Δslarp is to our knowledge the first completely attenuated rodent mutant in which multiple genes have been deleted that are critical for two independent biological processes during liver-stage development, that is regulation of parasite genes/transcripts that play a role in early liver-stage development stages (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011) and the establishment of the PV within the infected hepatocyte (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and citations to prior work (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011; Annoura et al., 2014).

claim: SLARP is involved in regulation of parasite genes/transcripts that play a role in early liver-stage development stages.
source: PbΔb9Δslarp is to our knowledge the first completely attenuated rodent mutant in which multiple genes have been deleted that are critical for two independent biological processes during liver-stage development, that is regulation of parasite genes/transcripts that play a role in early liver-stage development stages (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011) and the establishment of the PV within the infected hepatocyte (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011).

claim: B9 is involved in the establishment of the PV within the infected hepatocyte.
source: PbΔb9Δslarp is to our knowledge the first completely attenuated rodent mutant in which multiple genes have been deleted that are critical for two independent biological processes during liver-stage development, that is regulation of parasite genes/transcripts that play a role in early liver-stage development stages (Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011) and the establishment of the PV within the infected hepatocyte (Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014).

claim: A critical safety requirement for GAPs in order to qualify as vaccine candidate is the total absence of blood infections during immunization.
source: A critical safety requirement for GAPs in order to qualify as vaccine candidate is the total absence of blood infections during immunization and therefore the complete abrogation of liver-stage development.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about vaccine safety requirements.

claim: Many target genes including p52, p36, and those involved in type II fatty acid synthesis show a leaky phenotype, resulting in blood stage infections after administration of high number of sporozoites.
source: Unfortunately many of the above mentioned target genes including p52, p36, and those involved in type II fatty acid synthesis show a leaky phenotype, resulting in blood stage infections after administration of high number of sporozoites.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work mentioned earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Incomplete liver-stage arrest disqualifies GAPs for further clinical development for safety reasons.
source: Incomplete liver-stage arrest obviously disqualifies GAPs for further clinical development for safety reasons.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference about safety requirements for clinical development.

claim: The Pf GAP PfΔp52Δp36 was not completely attenuated in the Pb rodent model.
source: In the Pb rodent model, this GAP was not completely attenuated (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012).

claim: A low percentage of parasites of PfΔp52Δp36 GAP are able to develop into mature liver-stage.
source: Similarly, this Pf GAP while severely attenuated by the lack of both genes, a low percentage of parasites of this GAP are able to develop into mature liver-stage (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012).

claim: P52 and P36 have a partially redundant function.
source: These observations indicate a partially redundant function for these proteins; indeed, a breakthrough blood infection was observed in one out of the six volunteers after exposure to the bite of mosquitoes infected with sporozoites of a PfΔp52Δp36 GAP (Spring et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that deletion of both genes does not completely attenuate the parasite.

claim: A breakthrough blood infection was observed in one out of the six volunteers after exposure to the bite of mosquitoes infected with sporozoites of a PfΔp52Δp36 GAP.
source: These observations indicate a partially redundant function for these proteins; indeed, a breakthrough blood infection was observed in one out of the six volunteers after exposure to the bite of mosquitoes infected with sporozoites of a PfΔp52Δp36 GAP (Spring et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Spring et al., 2013).

claim: Functional redundancy of related genes has been reported in Plasmodium.
source: Since functional redundancy of related genes has been reported more often in Plasmodium (Liu et al., 2006; Heiss et al., 2008; van Dijk et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2013), we pursued the generation of GAPs from which multiple genes were removed from the genome, each governing a critical yet independent cellular process.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Liu et al., 2006; Heiss et al., 2008; van Dijk et al., 2010; Lin et al., 2013).

claim: P. falciparum mutants lacking FAS II enzymes fail to generate sporozoites inside the oocyst.
source: The selection of those target genes excluded type II fatty acid synthesis (FAS II) because P. falciparum mutants lacking FAS II enzymes fail to generate sporozoites inside the oocyst, indicating that the FAS II pathway is essential for sporogony (van Schaijk et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (van Schaijk et al., 2013).

claim: The FAS II pathway is essential for sporogony in P. falciparum.
source: The selection of those target genes excluded type II fatty acid synthesis (FAS II) because P. falciparum mutants lacking FAS II enzymes fail to generate sporozoites inside the oocyst, indicating that the FAS II pathway is essential for sporogony (van Schaijk et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (van Schaijk et al., 2013).

claim: No orthologues of LSA-1 are present in rodent or non-human primate Plasmodium species.
source: The gene encoding liver-stage antigen 1 (LSA-1) may be an attractive candidate, but no orthologues are present in rodent or non-human primate Plasmodium species precluding sufficient pre-clinical testing (Mikolajczak et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Mikolajczak et al., 2011).

claim: Unequivocal orthologues of uis3 or uis4 are absent in the P. falciparum genome.
source: The reverse is true for two published rodent GAPs with deletions of the genes uis3 or uis4 of which unequivocal orthologues are absent in the P. falciparum genome.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about gene orthology.

claim: Induction of protection by late arresting GAPs may be superior to early arresting GAPs.
source: Alternatively, genes encoding proteins with a role in the late stage parasite liver development could be an attractive target, since induction of protection by late arresting GAPs may be superior to early arresting GAPs (Butler et al., 2011; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013) However, late arresting GAPs are likely more risky and prone to breakthrough infection as shown for GAPs lacking the genes palm or lisp (Khan et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Butler et al., 2011; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013).

claim: Late arresting GAPs are likely more risky and prone to breakthrough infection.
source: Alternatively, genes encoding proteins with a role in the late stage parasite liver development could be an attractive target, since induction of protection by late arresting GAPs may be superior to early arresting GAPs (Butler et al., 2011; Nganou-Makamdop and Sauerwein, 2013) However, late arresting GAPs are likely more risky and prone to breakthrough infection as shown for GAPs lacking the genes palm or lisp (Khan et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Khan et al., 2012) showing breakthrough infections for palm and lisp GAPs.

claim: PbΔb9 elicits long-lived protective immune responses in mice.
source: PbΔb9 elicits long-lived protective immune responses in mice and only few breakthrough blood infections occur in mice, albeit less than were observed with PbΔp52Δp36 GAP sporozoites (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012) and data in Table 1.

claim: Only few breakthrough blood infections occur in mice with PbΔb9, less than were observed with PbΔp52Δp36 GAP sporozoites.
source: PbΔb9 elicits long-lived protective immune responses in mice and only few breakthrough blood infections occur in mice, albeit less than were observed with PbΔp52Δp36 GAP sporozoites (Annoura et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2012).

claim: The genes p52, p36, and b9 all belong to the 6-Cys family of Plasmodium proteins.
source: The genes p52, p36, and b9, all belong to the recently expanded 6-Cys family of Plasmodium proteins and may share a similar function in formation or maintenance of the PV membrane at the interface of parasite and host cell.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about these proteins.

claim: P52, P36, and B9 may share a similar function in formation or maintenance of the PV membrane at the interface of parasite and host cell.
source: The genes p52, p36, and b9, all belong to the recently expanded 6-Cys family of Plasmodium proteins and may share a similar function in formation or maintenance of the PV membrane at the interface of parasite and host cell.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on their membership in the same protein family.

claim: A triple gene-deletion mutant lacking p52, p36, and b9 is no more attenuated than a mutant lacking b9.
source: Indeed, a triple gene-deletion mutant lacking p52, p36, and b9 is no more attenuated than a mutant lacking b9, suggesting that these genes do not drive independent biological pathways (van Dijk et al., 2005; Ploemen et al., 2012; Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (van Dijk et al., 2005; Ploemen et al., 2012; Annoura et al., 2014).

claim: P52, P36, and B9 do not drive independent biological pathways.
source: Indeed, a triple gene-deletion mutant lacking p52, p36, and b9 is no more attenuated than a mutant lacking b9, suggesting that these genes do not drive independent biological pathways (van Dijk et al., 2005; Ploemen et al., 2012; Annoura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that the triple mutant is no more attenuated than the single b9 mutant.

claim: The early arresting slarp mutant is the only rodent GAP with a Pf ortholog without a record of breakthrough blood infections in mice.
source: To date, the early arresting slarp mutant is the only rodent GAP with a Pf ortholog without a record of breakthrough blood infections in mice.
evidence: The claim is based on review of the literature and experimental data in Table 2.

claim: Rodent sporozoites lacking slarp are fully capable of hepatocyte invasion and formation of a PV but completely abort development soon after invasion.
source: Indeed, our data confirm that rodent sporozoites lacking slarp are fully capable of hepatocyte invasion and formation of a PV but completely abort development soon after invasion as previously reported (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to prior work (Aly et al., 2008; Silvie et al., 2008; Aly et al., 2011).

claim: P. falciparum mutants lacking slarp completely arrest at day 3 post-infection of primary human hepatocytes.
source: In this study, we report for the first time that P. falciparum mutants lacking slarp, that is PfΔslarp, completely arrest at day 3 post-infection of primary human hepatocytes, while morphologically normal liver-stage parasites are still observed at 48 hpi.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Morphologically normal liver-stage parasites of PfΔslarp are still observed at 48 hpi in primary human hepatocytes.
source: In this study, we report for the first time that P. falciparum mutants lacking slarp, that is PfΔslarp, completely arrest at day 3 post-infection of primary human hepatocytes, while morphologically normal liver-stage parasites are still observed at 48 hpi.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The multiple attenuated PbΔb9Δslarp passed stringent pre-clinical safety screen with no breakthrough blood infections observed in all conditions tested.
source: The multiple attenuated PbΔb9Δslarp indeed passed our stringent pre-clinical safety screen and no breakthrough blood infections were observed in all conditions tested.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: Immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites induced strong and sustained protective immunity in BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice.
source: In addition, we showed that immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites induced strong and sustained protective immunity in BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice, with similar efficacy as reported for mutant sporozoites lacking P52 (or P52 and P36) or γ-radiated sporozoites (Nussenzweig et al., 1967; van Dijk et al., 2005; Douradinha et al., 2007; Labaied et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Table 1 and citations to prior work (Nussenzweig et al., 1967; van Dijk et al., 2005; Douradinha et al., 2007; Labaied et al., 2007).

claim: The efficacy of PbΔb9Δslarp immunization is similar to that reported for mutant sporozoites lacking P52 (or P52 and P36) or γ-radiated sporozoites.
source: In addition, we showed that immunization with PbΔb9Δslarp sporozoites induced strong and sustained protective immunity in BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice, with similar efficacy as reported for mutant sporozoites lacking P52 (or P52 and P36) or γ-radiated sporozoites (Nussenzweig et al., 1967; van Dijk et al., 2005; Douradinha et al., 2007; Labaied et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Nussenzweig et al., 1967; van Dijk et al., 2005; Douradinha et al., 2007; Labaied et al., 2007).

claim: Safety issues concerning the medical as well as environmental aspects must be considered for live vaccine strains including the absence of heterologous DNA sequences from the genome of GAPs.
source: Live vaccine strains (attenuated by natural selection or genetic engineering) may be potentially released into the environment. Therefore, safety issues concerning the medical as well as environmental aspects must be considered including the absence of heterologous DNA sequences (in particular drug resistance genes) from the genome of GAPs (Committee for Medical Products for Human Use, 2006; Frey, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to regulatory guidance (Committee for Medical Products for Human Use, 2006; Frey, 2007).

claim: FRT/FLPe-recombinase methodology permits the removal of drug resistance markers introduced to generate the mutant.
source: This approach permits the removal of drug resistance markers that were introduced to generate the mutant and results in an altered genome that retains only two 34 nucleotide FRT sequences.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the FRT/FLPe recombinase system.

claim: The FRT/FLPe-recombinase methodology results in an altered genome that retains only two 34 nucleotide FRT sequences.
source: This approach permits the removal of drug resistance markers that were introduced to generate the mutant and results in an altered genome that retains only two 34 nucleotide FRT sequences.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about the FRT/FLPe recombinase system.

claim: The removal of the drug resistance marker has the advantage that these parasites are easily amenable to further genetic modification.
source: The removal of the drug resistance marker has the additional advantage that these parasites are easily amenable to further genetic modification (van Schaijk et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (van Schaijk et al., 2010).

claim: The PfΔb9Δslarp GAP aborted early development in cultured primary human hepatocytes, with a phenotype and timing similar to PfΔb9.
source: The PfΔb9Δslarp GAP aborted early development in cultured primary human hepatocytes, with a phenotype and timing similar to PfΔb9, and studies performed in a limited number of chimeric mice engrafted with human hepatocytes confirm this arrest phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Studies performed in chimeric mice engrafted with human hepatocytes confirm the arrest phenotype of PfΔb9Δslarp.
source: The PfΔb9Δslarp GAP aborted early development in cultured primary human hepatocytes, with a phenotype and timing similar to PfΔb9, and studies performed in a limited number of chimeric mice engrafted with human hepatocytes confirm this arrest phenotype.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Δb9 attenuation phenotype induces highly effective protection.
source: From the combined Pb and Pf data, one can conclude that Δb9 attenuation phenotype induces highly effective protection, although it may at a low frequency produce a breakthrough blood infection.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the combined experimental data.

claim: Δb9 attenuation may at a low frequency produce a breakthrough blood infection.
source: From the combined Pb and Pf data, one can conclude that Δb9 attenuation phenotype induces highly effective protection, although it may at a low frequency produce a breakthrough blood infection.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior work (Annoura et al., 2014) showing occasional breakthrough infections.

claim: The additional deletion of slarp in Δb9 mutants provides these parasites with complete attenuation that is essential in order to proceed with human trials.
source: Therefore, the additional deletion of slarp in these mutants provides these parasites with complete attenuation that is essential in order to proceed with human trials.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing no breakthrough infections with the double mutant.

claim: Production of PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites is unabated and similar to WT parasites.
source: An important prerequisite for further downstream clinical development and manufacturing (Seder et al., 2013) is to show that production of PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites is unabated and similar to WT parasites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PfΔb9Δslarp GAP produces WT numbers of sporozoites that are fully capable of infecting hepatocytes.
source: We have shown that the PfΔb9Δslarp GAP produces WT numbers of sporozoites that are fully capable of infecting hepatocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 3A.

claim: Aseptic, purified, cryopreserved PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites have been produced.
source: In addition, we have produced aseptic, purified, cryopreserved PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated but data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: None of the PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites developed to mature liver-stage parasites expressing PfMSP-1 in a 6-day attenuation assay in HC-04 cells.
source: Preliminary data from a 6-day attenuation assay in HC-04 cells showed that like irradiated PfSPZ (Hoffman et al., 2010; Epstein et al., 2011), none of the PfΔb9Δslarp sporozoites developed to mature liver-stage parasites expressing PfMSP-1 (data not shown), as aseptic, purified, cryopreserved WT sporozoites (Roestenberg et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated but data is not shown in the manuscript, and is compared to prior work (Hoffman et al., 2010; Epstein et al., 2011; Roestenberg et al., 2013).
